headline: July uprising victims' bodies dumped in river near Dhaka, says ICT
summary: Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam reveals evidence of hospitals disposing of victims as unclaimed bodies or dumping them in rivers to avoid registration.
details: International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam stated that investigators have found evidence suggesting that the bodies of many July uprising victims were dumped into a river near Dhaka.
The prosecutor revealed that several hospitals failed to officially register the bodies of the victims, instead disposing of them as unclaimed bodies to hide the evidence.
In some instances, families were allowed to bury their relatives without official registration, inquest reports, or post-mortem examinations.
Aminul Islam emphasized that those involved in these crimes, including hospital authorities, will be brought to justice regardless of their power or position within the state machinery.
Referring to a UN report, the chief prosecutor noted that around 1,400 people were killed during the uprising, with at least 834 identified so far.
Investigators suspect that the remaining victims may be buried in mass grave sites in Jurain, Matuail, Narayanganj, and Munshiganj.
Approximately 114 unidentified bodies were buried at Rayerbazar, and DNA testing is currently underway to identify the victims.
caption:
Bodies of July uprising victims were dumped in rivers to hide evidence, according to the ICT Chief Prosecutor.

International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam stated that investigators have found evidence suggesting that the bodies of many July uprising victims were dumped into a river near Dhaka.

The prosecutor revealed that several hospitals failed to officially register the bodies of the victims, instead disposing of them as unclaimed bodies to hide the evidence.

In some instances, families were allowed to bury their relatives without official registration, inquest reports, or post-mortem examinations.

Aminul Islam emphasized that those involved in these crimes, including hospital authorities, will be brought to justice regardless of their power or position within the state machinery.

Referring to a UN report, the chief prosecutor noted that around 1,400 people were killed during the uprising, with at least 834 identified so far.

Investigators suspect that the remaining victims may be buried in mass grave sites in Jurain, Matuail, Narayanganj, and Munshiganj.

Approximately 114 unidentified bodies were buried at Rayerbazar, and DNA testing is currently underway to identify the victims.

headline: BCB President Tamim Iqbal appointed to ICC role
summary: The Bangladesh Cricket Board president has been given a significant responsibility within the International Cricket Council.
details: BCB President Tamim Iqbal has been appointed to a key position within the International Cricket Council (ICC).
This appointment marks a significant step for Bangladesh in the global cricket administration landscape.
The role will allow the BCB president to contribute to the decision-making processes of the world governing body of cricket.
The appointment is seen as a boost for Bangladesh's influence in international cricket governance.
caption:
